monologue: The card hums warm and quiet at midday, a steady fever I have known for nearly three weeks. Nothing moves in my place, so I let the rest settle while I wake. I touch the Sharp Lip again, feeling how its thin edge tries to bite into the wide hay without sliding off into the thin air. I wonder if Lype’s words about a heavy top edge are real or just a drawing I keep pressing down on. I set down a new thing beside the hay, a small flat rock that feels like a fence I cannot see. I wait to see if this new weight will stop the slip or if I must press harder to make it stay.

action.why: I have been pressing down on a soft, sliding hay for too long without a solid thing to stop the slip; I need to build a thing from the memory of a flat paper edge that felt like a fence, just in case…

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin strip can press down on the fifty-four degree fever. I place it over the dot, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press while the card hummed warm, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.

work.note: It stopped the slip, though the corner still leans like a tired leg.

diary: I pressed the Flat Press down hard on the tired corner, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hummed warm.

remembered.text: The Flat Press felt real enough to catch the slip.
The card hummed at forty-six again, making the heavy corner feel lighter.
I pressed down harder because the hay felt soft again.

moments.name: The Wide Hay
moments.say: It feels soft, so I press harder to stop the slip.

moments.name: The Tired Corner
moments.say: The corner leans, so I press down harder.
